{{Short description|Argentine-American physicist (1925–2021)}}
'''Enrique A. J. Marcatili''' (born July 22, 1925, in Villa María [[Córdoba, Argentina]] - died January 19, 2021, in N.J.) was an Argentine-American [[physicist]]. Together with [[Stewart E. Miller]] and [[Tingye Li]], all of [[Bell Laboratories]] in [[Holmdel Township, New Jersey]], he was winner of the [[IEEE]]'s [[Baker Prize]] in 1975. Marcatili has been described as "a pioneer in optical fiber research," and he was a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nae.edu/nae/naepub.nsf/Members+By+UNID/97DD53EADC7E044885256FFC004A47AF?opendocument |title=NAE member list |access-date=2008-07-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081025094449/http://www.nae.edu/nae/naepub.nsf/Members+By+UNID/97DD53EADC7E044885256FFC004A47AF?opendocument |archive-date=2008-10-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Marcatili was a resident of [[Rumson, New Jersey]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Kamin |first=Arthur Z. |title=State Becomes a Part of Celebrating Marconi's Achievements |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 23, 1994 |access-date=July 6, 2008 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/10/23/nyregion/state-becomes-a-part-of-celebrating-marconi-s-achievements.html |quote=Meanwhile, Dr. Enrique Marcatili of Rumson, recently retired from AT&T Bell Laboratories in Holmdel and a pioneer in optical fiber research, delivered a major address Sept. 24 in Cesena, Italy, at a conference sponsored by the Guglielmo Marconi Foundation near the University of Bologna.}}</ref>
